articles.title: 2026 NFL Roster Cuts: Predicting the Biggest Names Who Could Hit the Market
articles.summary: It's a nerve-wracking time of year for many NFL players.
articles.body:
It's a nerve-wracking time of year for many NFL players.

As the preseason winds down and the start of the regular season approaches, NFL teams have difficult decisions to make. By the time we hit 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, all 32 teams have to cut their active rosters to 53 players.

As many as 1,184 players will be released, return their playbooks and attempt to secure practice-squad spots.

Every year, there are some surprising departures. Some are early-round picks who just haven't panned out, veterans who are released as much for economics as performance, and aging vets at the end of the line.

Here are some of the biggest names who could get cut before the deadline.

Quarterbacks generally retain value around the NFL, so it's a bit odd to imagine a team cutting bait on a young signal-caller who made six starts in 2025.

However, Cleveland's crowded quarterback room makes Gabriel's path to a roster spot increasingly uncertain.

Gabriel barely played in the Browns' second preseason game, failing to complete his only pass attempt. But he was on the field for three false starts, drawing the ire of head coach Todd Monken after the game :

"At the end, you wanna talk about (expletive) football. I don't care who goes out there. If I could have taken a knee, I probably would have. What the (expletive)? I don't know what to tell you. We work on cadence and operation, and we will continue to do it. You can't lead an offense if you can't lead a cadence. Browns hurting Browns. You're not going to have a chance when you do that."

Gabriel was a third-round pick of the Browns in 2025, but for better or worse he has clearly fallen behind Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson on the depth chart. With rookie Taylen Green also on the roster, it's a numbers game—one Gabriel is losing.

This isn't to say Gabriel won't land with another team, or that he can't carve out a lengthy career in the NFL as a backup quarterback. But it is becoming increasingly apparent that his next opportunity will come elsewhere.

Not long ago, the Arizona Cardinals hoped Trey Benson would become their lead running back.

Now, it's looking more and more like he won't even be on their 53-man roster.

Benson has flashed at times when healthy, but that "when healthy" caveat has been a big one—the third-round pick in 2024 missed time as a rookie with an ankle injury and made it just four games into the 2025 campaign before a knee issue ended his season.

That same knee injury has hampered the 24-year-old this offseason, although Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur attempted to downplay the injury:

"Just a little discomfort, just a little flare up in the left knee. It's unfortunate because it was feeling so good and I really thought he was getting his legs underneath him. Any time you're coming back from an injury like him, he just wants to be out there. He can feel everything going up and then all of (a) sudden out of nowhere, it kind of just flared up on him a little bit."

After drafting Jeremiyah Love third overall in April, there's no question who the lead back in the desert is. The team also has a high-end No. 2 back after signing Tyler Allgeier in free agency.

Given that, Benson's spot on the roster was already shaky. His inability to stay healthy may well have sealed his fate.

The first pick in the second round of the 2023 draft, Will Levis made 21 starts over his first two seasons. Then the Titans drafted Cam Ward first overall in 2025, and Levis was relegated to the bench.

The Kentucky product may soon be out of Nashville altogether.

For his part, Levis told reporters that he still believes he can be a capable starter under center in the NFL:

"I know I've put the tape out there already that I'm a dang good quarterback in this league and I'm even better than I ever have been. There are not 32 quarterbacks in this league better than me. I know that for sure. I'm just focused on having fun. I needed that time, not just physically, but just mentally to calm the nervous system. Where I'm at mentally is in a much healthier place than it's ever been. I feel like I worked a lot for other people's approval in the beginning of my career. And whereas I'm just trying to be the best version of me at this point."

Levis, 27, may not be lacking in confidence, but his performance tells another story. In those 21 starts, he threw just 21 touchdown passes. His passer rating barely cracked 80, and he committed multiple turnovers.

Ward is the unquestioned starter in Tennessee, while Mitchell Trubisky is a veteran backup with nine seasons and 57 starts under his belt.

Levis faces a difficult path to a roster spot.

Sam Williams once appeared to be an ascending young edge-rusher for the Dallas Cowboys.

A second-round pick in 2022, he amassed 8.5 sacks over the first two years of his career. But injury wiped out his 2024 season, and he had just one sack despite playing a career-high 474 snaps a year ago.

Williams told reporters that he has heard all those who doubt his ability to make an impact in the NFL—and he has used that as fuel to have his best season yet:

"I took all the reports, all the negative comments, everything. And I took it in and I looked at myself in the mirror because you can't get better unless you know what you're doing wrong. So, everything that I've seen, I try to fix. Like even in my room, it's written on the mirror. At the end of the day, I just took all the negatives and, you know, look myself in the mirror. Not blaming no one else and just work. Just work, work, work. Put my head down and let my work speak for itself."

Williams may have to jump-start his career elsewhere. Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeiruaku, rookie Malachi Lawrence and newly signed Von Miller appear to be locks for the 53-man roster. That could leave only one or two spots for Williams, Marist Liufau and James Houston, and Liufau is a core special teams contributor.

Williams would no doubt quickly get scooped up, but the truth is there may not be room for him in Dallas anymore.

When the Kansas City Chiefs signed cornerback Kristian Fulton last year, it was supposed to be a stabilizing move—a veteran presence added to the position group a year before what became a seismic shift in personnel.

As Matt Conner noted for Arrowhead Addict , however, that isn't exactly what happened:

"Instead of providing a dependable pillar in the midst of change, everything about Fulton has been perplexing from his first preseason. Not only did he miss the bulk of training camp due to injury, but he also hurt his ankle early in Week 2. By the time he was healthy, he still wasn't playing as a healthy scratch week after week for Steve Spagnuolo's defense."

Now, there's a real chance Fulton could be out of a job altogether.

Rookie first-rounder Mansoor Delane appears likely to start on the boundary, while Nohl Williams and L'Jarius Sneed are the leading candidates for the other outside role. With Kader Kohou projected to handle slot duties, Fulton could enter the season as Kansas City's fourth cornerback, assuming Spagnuolo views him more favorably than he did last year.

Fulton wasn't terrible when he was on the field—his 81.7 passer rating against was his best since 2021—but he played just 208 snaps in his first season in Kansas City. And a $13 million cap hit is a lot for a subpackage corner.

Odell Beckham Jr. was once arguably the NFL's best wide receiver during his time with the New York Giants.

In each of his first three seasons, he topped 1,300 receiving yards. He made one of the greatest catches of all time and won a Super Bowl with the Los Angeles Rams.

Beckham is now nearing his 34th birthday, though, and his last 1,000-yard season came back in 2019. Last year in Miami, he caught all of nine passes for 55 yards.

And while a reunion with the team where he started his career may be a good story, Beckham faces an uphill battle to make the Week 1 roster, according to ESPN's Jordan Ranaan :

"Beckham is clearly on the bubble. Malik Nabers, Darnell Mooney and Braxton Berrios all had the day off in Saturday's preseason game against the Dolphins. Malachi Fields, Darius Slayton and Calvin Austin III started. Beckham is behind them all on the depth chart. Beckham has proven he can get open, but is that enough? Unless the Giants trade a wide receiver, there probably won't be room for him on the roster."

Beckham didn't help his chances by narrowly missing a touchdown catch in that game against the Dolphins, but the reality is that he's an aging receiver who has one year with 550 receiving yards in the last six years.

His recent production has not matched the reputation he built earlier in his career.

articles.title: NFL's Biggest Rumors and Latest Buzz Ahead of 2026 Roster Cuts Deadline
articles.summary: NFL coaches have enough game film and training camp practice evaluations to make key roster decisions before the August 30 cutdown deadline. It's going to be a busy week.
articles.body:
NFL coaches have enough game film and training camp practice evaluations to make key roster decisions before the August 30 cutdown deadline. It's going to be a busy week.

While some players continue to battle for roster spots in the final week of the preseason, coaches will be in their offices looking over the dynamics of prospective depth charts for the regular season.

To get an idea of what could happen in the coming days, let's check in with the latest buzz on potential cuts, trades and roster news.

Who are the notable veterans on the roster bubble? Who might be on the trade block? What are some team concerns ahead of Week 1?

Bills' Notable Free-Agent Acquisitions Are on the Roster Bubble

The Buffalo Bills signed safety Geno Stone and outside linebacker Mike Danna to one-year deals. They've both held starting roles over the last few years with their previous teams.

With the Kansas City Chiefs, Danna worked his way into a lead position at defensive end. Stone earned a first-string role with the Baltimore Ravens in 2023 and started in every game with the Cincinnati Bengals between 2024 and 2025.

But the Bills have a stacked roster. Consequently, Stone and Danna are cut candidates ahead of the deadline.

The Athletic's Joe Buscaglia explained why he left Danna off his latest Bills 53-man roster projection:

" Mike Danna, an early May signing, has over $1 million guaranteed on his one-year deal, but he's faded into the background in the outside linebacker group. With investments in Hoecht, Parker a roster lock and Solomon as one of their best special teams assets, I've got Danna on the outside of this projection ."

Buscaglia believes the Bills could make a decision between Damar Hamlin and Stone at safety, with the former having a slight edge in a battle for one spot.

"While I still have the Bills keeping five safeties, I've switched Hamlin onto the 53-man roster and Stone on the outside looking in," Buscaglia wrote. "Between the two, I think Hamlin has been the more consistent player."

As former starters still younger than 30, Danna and Stone will likely land with new teams before Week 1 if the Bills cut them.

Bengals Might Add Help at Offensive Tackle

The Cincinnati Bengals haven't settled on a primary swing tackle.

After last Saturday's preseason game against the Chicago Bears, head coach Zac Taylor shared his thoughts on the position via Kelsey Conway of the Cincinnati Enquirer .

"I think that's still pretty open," Taylor said. "I think there's guys we're still looking at and I wouldn't say there's any decisions we've made there."

Conway believes the Bengals could be in the market for an offensive tackle after final roster cuts, and it could impact Cody Ford's standing on the depth chart:

" The Bengals could very well be in the market for a reserve tackle over the next few weeks when roster cuts begin around the NFL. It's unlikely the Bengals will move on from Ford ahead of the season because of his experience in the offense, but this doesn't mean if the pro personnel department finds a better option, he wouldn't lose his spot ."

Orlando Brown Jr. and Amarius Mims are the Bengals' starting tackles on the left and right side, respectively. They both started in every game last season but struggled in pass protection.

According to Pro Football Focus, Brown allowed nine sacks over 733 pass-blocking snaps, and Mims allowed 35 pressures over 694 pass-blocking snaps.

The Bengals aren't at a point of benching either of them, but they need reliable reinforcements to protect quarterback Joe Burrow if injuries and/or further decline in performance cost the starters playing time.

Browns TE Dae'Quan Wright Could Become First NFL Player to Return to College

Dae'Quan Wright could be the first to return to the college ranks after an offseason in the NFL.

This year, Wright went undrafted and signed with the Philadelphia Eagles, who waived him on August 10. The Cleveland Browns claimed him, then waived the 22-year-old on Sunday.

Wright's agents, Drew Rosenhaus and Kyle Lincoln, told ESPN's Adam Schefter that their client has an agreement to play at LSU for the 2026 term.

Wright dressed for the Browns' second preseason game, but he didn't play a snap. After the contest, head coach Todd Monken briefly discussed the situation around the rookie tight end.

"Man, isn't this s--t crazy?" Monken said Saturday . "I don't even know what to say. I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out to me a week ago; now I know. I didn't call him back. I guess I should have."

Going forward, we could see more undrafted rookies follow the same pathway as Wright if they're unable to secure roster spots.

Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty Is Nursing a Sprained Ankle

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter, Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty sprained his ankle at practice on Sunday.

The Athletic's Sam Warren provided context to the incident in a post on X:

" Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty left practice early today with an apparent injury. He dove for a ball that was beyond him during team period and went down awkwardly. He was helped off the field by trainers, unable to put weight on his right leg and he did not return ."

Warren also noted rookie fourth-rounder Mike Washington Jr. picked up most of the carries in Jeanty's absence.

With a strong showing at camp and two productive preseason outings, logging 15 carries for 119 yards, Washington has likely earned more touches regardless of Jeanty's status.

Though Jeanty avoided a significant injury, his return timetable remains unclear. The Raiders may ask a little more of Washington if their lead ball-carrier is sidelined for the start of the regular season. They could also add to the running back room to strengthen a backfield platoon.

J.J. McCarthy May Fall to QB3 on Vikings Depth Chart, Trade Questions Brewing

The Minnesota Vikings declared Kyler Murray their starter over J.J. McCarthy early in a quarterback competition.

Head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters that McCarthy still has a "future with the organization" via ESPN's Kevin Seifert . But the third-year signal-caller's short-term outlook is uncertain.

During an ESPN SportsCenter segment (h/t X user @realmnsportsfan), Jeremy Fowler suggested McCarthy may not even be Murray's primary backup and brought up the possibility of a trade.

"Is he QB2 in Minnesota or is he QB3? Because they do have Carson Wentz," Fowler said. "So, could the Minnesota Vikings field a few trade calls? A lot could happen. They have to decide what McCarthy's role is on the team."

After completing 57.6 percent of his passes last season, McCarthy has struggled with his accuracy and ball placement in the preseason. In his last outing against the Baltimore Ravens, he threw a pinpoint 50-yard laser to wideout Tai Felton but failed to connect with wideout Myles Price on a wide-open throw to the end zone and finished with a 50 percent completion rate.

McCarthy's standing on Minnesota's depth chart would become more uncertain if the Vikings list Wentz as their No. 2 quarterback.

Patriots HC Mike Vrabel Blunt About Lack of Roster Depth

NFL teams need reliable backups who can fill in for banged-up starters. In many cases, the healthiest top clubs make deep playoff runs.

Head coach Mike Vrabel gave an honest assessment of his roster's depth and why it was important to protect his starters in the preseason via ESPN's Mike Reiss .

"I do not think we have a very deep team, so I think we have to make sure that we are preparing our football team and that we are doing everything that we can to keep our best players available," Vrabel said.

Coming off a Super Bowl loss, New England bolstered its starting unit, adding wideouts A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, guard Alijah Vera-Tucker, outside linebacker Dre'Mont Jones and safety Kevin Byard, but the roster still lacks experienced reinforcements outside of the wide receiver and offensive line groups.

If the Patriots have to work around a rash of injuries, it could be a major issue late in the upcoming season. They may be one of the more active teams in acquiring players after roster cuts.

Steelers Might Retain 4 Quarterbacks on 53-Man Roster

The Pittsburgh Steelers may hoard quarterback talent and retain all four of their signal-callers.

Mason Rudolph didn't play in the second preseason game, which is an indication that he's Aaron Rodgers' primary backup, unless the team trades him.

Drew Allar had an impressive preseason debut, going 10-of-13 passing for 153 yards and two touchdowns with a rushing score, but he completed less than 50 percent of his passes last week in a 17-0 loss to the New York Jets. Will Howard struggled in the previous outing, throwing two interceptions.

Allar and Howard probably aren't ready for fill-in duty if Rodgers goes down with an injury, which is why Pittsburgh should keep Rudolph.

ESPN's Brooke Pryor believes the Steelers might trim their offensive line or safeties groups to keep four quarterbacks:

" Unless the Steelers try to sneak Howard through on the practice squad, it seems more and more likely that they'll keep four quarterbacks, and that would mean numbers have to be reduced somewhere else on the roster. Two potential groups to watch are the offensive linemen and safeties because of the position flexibility of veterans such as Brock Hoffman and Jalen Ramsey ."

If the Steelers expose one of their signal-callers to waivers, Howard is the name to watch ahead of the roster cuts deadline.

Howard, a sixth-round pick in the 2025 draft, spent most of his rookie year recovering from a fractured pinky on his throwing hand.

As a rookie third-rounder who's shown some flashes, Allar should be a priority developmental project for the future.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton .

articles.title: Buying or Selling the Top NFL Performers of Preseason Week 2
articles.summary: Though it didn't bring as much excitement as the regular season ultimately will, Week 2 of the NFL preseason was quite a bit of fun. Not every game was competitive, of course, but the most recent slate of exhibition games brought some thrilling standout performances.
articles.body:
Though it didn't bring as much excitement as the regular season ultimately will, Week 2 of the NFL preseason was quite a bit of fun. Not every game was competitive, of course, but the most recent slate of exhibition games brought some thrilling standout performances.

Of course, it's important to consume strong preseason performances with a grain of salt. Players are rarely playing with or against a full complement of starters and are frequently operating in the most basic of schemes. Some performances, while impressive, prove to be a mirage.

Last year, for example, Chris Blair led the NFL in preseason receiving yards and went on to play a mere 12 offensive snaps for the Atlanta Falcons.

Here, we'll dive into some of the biggest standout performances of preseason Week 2 and buy or sell each outing based on factors like game situations, past performances, projected 2026 role, and overall player expectations.

Dallas Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton III had a fantastic outing against a bad Arizona Cardinals defense, finishing with 179 passing yards, two passing touchdowns, and a rushing score. He also made several eye-catching throws on Saturday evening.

However, the Cowboys are still leaving the competition for their backup QB job open for now.

"This is long from over," head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters after the game (h/t ProFootballTalk's Josh Alper ).

However, Milton's Week 2 display should be enough to earn him the nod over Sam Howell to be Dak Prescott's understudy. The 2024 sixth-round pick out of Tennessee has long possessed impressive physical traits, and he's beginning to add some nuance, anticipation, and processing to his game.

The fact that Milton's latest performance came against an Arizona team that seemed largely uninterested in playing defense should not diminish his development. His combination of arm talent and running ability makes him a much better fit for Dallas' offense than Howell should either be called upon to play in the regular season.

Sell: Carson Steele, RB, Philadelphia Eagles

Milton wasn't the only NFC East backup to put on a show on Saturday. Philadelphia Eagles backup running back Carson Steele dropped jaws with not one, but two, instances of leaping over a defender.

His second hurdle came en route to the end zone and a go-ahead fourth-quarter score.

Steele finished with 33 rushing yards, 84 receiving yards, and the touchdown against the New England Patriots on Saturday. Was his outing a sign that the Eagles have a new offensive weapon who can spell Saquon Barkley?

Not exactly. While Steele certainly has the talent to provide depth behind Barkley, Tank Bigsby, and Will Shipley, he has never been a particularly efficient player in the NFL. He averaged just 3.3 yards per carry with the Kansas City Chiefs in 2024 and spent the next season on their practice squad.

The 6'0", 228-pound Steele may stick with Philly as an option at fullback, but he's going to be an offensive afterthought once the Eagles get to the regular season.

Buy: De'Zhaun Stribling, WR, San Francisco 49ers

During April's draft, the San Francisco 49ers traded down twice before taking Mississippi wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling 33rd overall.

While some viewed the selection as a reach—and, to be fair, Stribling was the 68th-ranked player on the Bleacher Report Scouting Department's final big board —the rookie is looking like a strong fit for San Francisco's offense.

During Thursday's 41-17 romp over the Los Angeles Chargers, Stribling tied for the team lead (with KhaDarel Hodge) in receptions and receiving yards while showcasing some big-play ability.

This marked the second strong preseason outing for Stribling, who had seven catches for 63 yards in San Francisco's preseason opener.

It would be silly to put too much stock in a receiver's numbers against backups and vanilla defenses. However, Stribling is probably poised for a strong rookie season. His combination of size (6'2", 207 lbs) and speed (4.36-second 40-yard dash) makes him well-suited for Kyle Shanahan's spacing-based passing attack, and it's not as if the 49ers are loaded with healthy receiver depth.

It's too early to be penciling in Stribling for Offensive Rookie of the Year. However, he should be walking into a substantial role, and it's not too early for 49ers fans to be excited about it.

Predicting When Injured Stars Will Debut

Sell: Colbie Young, WR, Cincinnati Bengals

Like Stribling, Cincinnati Bengals fourth-round pick Colbie Young is ready to have an instant impact as a rookie, right? Based on his performance on Saturday night, one might believe so.

The 6'4", 218-pound Georgia product logged three catches and led the Bengals with 48 receiving yards. He also used his size and ball skills to show what sort of red-zone threat he could be for Cincinnati.

However, while Stribling is likely to have a big role right away in San Francisco, Young will probably tumble down the depth chart once the regular season begins.

Sure, having a tall, big-bodied receiver can be beneficial near the goal line. However, the Bengals already have premium red-zone targets in Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Andrei Iosivas, and Mike Gesicki. The reality is that Young just isn't likely to see many opportunities in Cincinnati's offense this season.

Let's not forget that Mitchell Tinsley was a Bengals preseason darling in 2025, due in large part to his ability to make contested catches. He went on to record just eight receptions in the regular season.

Geno Smith officially made his New York Jets return on Friday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. While it's certainly worth noting that he primarily battled backups, his command of the offense and near-perfection during limited action is also noteworthy.

Smith was a perfect 7-of-7 on his lone drive against Pittsburgh, which he finished with a touchdown pass.

Now, look. We're talking about the Jets, and they're seemingly not allowed to have nice things at quarterback, so it's fair to be skeptical of Smith's performance. However, fans shouldn't be shocked if he makes the offense a lot of fun in 2026.

Smith was a two-time Pro Bowler with the Seattle Seahawks, and he's a great fit for Frank Reich's offense. Had he not spent last season on the sinking ship that was the Pete Carroll-led Las Vegas Raiders, Smith would probably be carrying much higher expectations in New York.

While Smith isn't going to be an MVP candidate or lead the Jets to the Super Bowl, he should perform well with a supporting cast now headlined by Olumuyiwa Fashanu, Garrett Wilson, Breece Hall, Kenyon Sadiq , and Omar Cooper Jr.

Sell: Shedeur Sanders, QB, Cleveland Browns

Editor's Note: The Browns named Deshaun Watson the starting QB on Monday.

While Smith is flying under the radar in New York, everything that Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders does seems to be magnified.

The second-year signal-caller out of Colorado was far from perfect against the Buffalo Bills on Saturday. However, he was largely solid while going 9-of-11 for 74 yards with one touchdown and one interception.

Sanders fans will be quick to point out that his interception was deflected out of his intended target's hands while his touchdown strike was on time and accurate.

However, a couple of mostly-good series against Buffalo backups doesn't mean that Sanders is ready to lead Cleveland to the postseason. It might not even be enough to put Sanders ahead of Deshaun Watson in the QB competition—even if Watson has become a frustratingly low bar to clear.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Browns plan to announce their Week 1 starter on Monday.

The difference between Smith and Sanders is that only one has shown that he can play at a consistently high level over the course of an NFL season. Sanders has only shown flashes, and while he could still develop into a quality starter for Cleveland, he's a long way away from being a franchise quarterback or making the Browns forget about the 2027 quarterback class.

Buy: Mike Washington, RB, Las Vegas Raiders

All eyes have been on Raiders quarterback and first overall pick Fernando Mendoza this summer, but he hasn't been the only Las Vegas rookie generating a bit of buzz. Fourth-round running back Mike Washington Jr. has flashed in practices and turned a few heads against the Houston Texans on Thursday.

Washington caught a pair of passes, logged a team-high 56 rushing yards, and continued to show his big-play ability.

Through two preseason games, Washington has racked up 119 rushing yards while averaging an impressive 7.9 yards per carry. Now, it's worth noting that his average has been significantly boosted by some long runs, but he's still been one of the preseason's most impressive ball-carriers.

The question, of course, is whether Las Vegas will have a role for Washington with 2025 first-round pick Ashton Jeanty leading the backfield. In all likelihood, it will.

New head coach Klint Kubiak used a committee approach as the Seahawks' offensive coordinator, and Washington's breakaway speed (4.33-second 40-yard dash) should make him an excellent complement to Jeanty.

And Washington can be more than just a speedy change of pace, as evidenced by the 28 receptions and 1,296 scrimmage yards he logged last season at Arkansas. Las Vegas may lean on him for the immediate future, as Jeanty suffered an injury in Sunday's practice and is believed to have a sprained ankle, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Washington wasn't the only fourth-round rookie who made the highlight reel in the Raiders-Texans game.

Houston linebacker Wade Woodaz made the play of the day when he picked off Mendoza and ran it back for an 80-yard pick-six.

While Woodaz's two tackles and big play may foreshadow what is to come, fans shouldn't expect him to be a Defensive Rookie of the Year candidate or an immediate IDP fantasy star.

A running back like Washington can easily slot into a specific role, especially on a rebuilding team that is hungry for talent. The Texans, however, are legitimate title contenders with two entrenched starting inside linebackers—Azeez Al-Shaair and Henry To'oTo'o—with a loaded defense overall.

Woodaz doesn't have a wide-open path to playing time, and it doesn't help that he's set to undergo surgery for a broken thumb, according to Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston.

While Woodaz could very well become a future star for the Texans, Thursday's preseason outing may be his last big game for a while.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel Addresses 'Issues' with Patriots Front Office After Calling Out Roster Depth
articles.summary: After surprisingly declaring that the New England Patriots are lacking depth entering the 2026 season, head coach Mike Vrabel clarified that there isn't a disconnect between him and the team's front office.
articles.body:
After surprisingly declaring that the New England Patriots are lacking depth entering the 2026 season, head coach Mike Vrabel clarified that there isn't a disconnect between him and the team's front office.

"These aren't issues. I'm not in a subtle context -- that wasn't that," Vrabel said Monday in his weekly appearance on sports radio WEEI, per ESPN's Mike Reiss . "They asked why we didn't play the guys, and [the answer is] we have to have everybody we have available and then continue to develop and see some guys that went out and played like they did on Saturday night to build that depth."

The concerns over Vrabel's relationship with New England's front office arose when the second-year coach candidly admitted that he held the defending AFC champion's starters out of the first two preseason games because he isn't confident in the depth of the roster.

"I do not think we have a very deep team, so I think we have to make sure that we are preparing our football team and that we are doing everything that we can to keep our best players available," he said after Saturday's 24-21 preseason win over the Philadelphia Eagles, per Reiss .

On Monday, Vrabel made it clear that he was not attempting to send a message or shift blame to anyone else in the organization, as he has been part of key roster decisions since taking over as head coach last year.

"We are the front office. We are all making the decisions. We're all included in this. It was about the young guys we have to develop," Vrabel said. "You can see that the players we kept out of the game, those are the guys. And we have to be able to find some guys behind them to be backups, to be the first guy in … those are the things that we are trying to develop and I guess that's what I was referencing."

The Patriots are hoping to contend for a second straight trip to the Super Bowl, but Vrabel's comments indicate that they may not be worthy of being projected among the elite teams in the NFL this season.

articles.summary: Week 2 of the NFL preseason slate is, by and large, the true test runs for teams ahead of the regular season.
articles.body:
Week 2 of the NFL preseason slate is, by and large, the true test runs for teams ahead of the regular season.

In a lot of ways, it serves the same function for fantasy football managers.

Ahead of the busiest draft weekend on the calendar, it offers the last real opportunity for cram-session studying. Maybe that's mock drafting, rankings analysis or team-name spitballing. Or perhaps it's seeking out an article like this featuring team names to consider, PPR rankings and draft advice for dynasty leagues.

Since dynasty leagues carry rosters over from one season to the next, the setup is as similar to running an NFL franchise as you'll find in the fantasy world. And much like NFL teams, dynasty leagues feature both win-now contenders and long-term rebuilders.

You need to know (and accept) your team's true identity and draft accordingly. If you have a realistic chance of winning big this season, then bump up those tried-and-true (and maybe a little boring) veterans. Safe, reliable production is your friend. Conversely, you should not be paying premiums for mystery-box rookies.

If you're on the other end of the competitive scale, then you should be throwing as many long-term darts as you can. They aren't all going to hit, so that's why you want as many lottery tickets as you can get. You only need a couple of big connections to significantly brighten your future and improve your odds of eventually finding your way to title town.

While injuries can knock out any players at any moment, the trend still shows they impact certain positions more consistently than others. That's especially true when thinking of longevity.

Running backs, by nature, tend to have pretty limited shelf lives. That's one of the biggest reasons caution flags are flying high around Christian McCaffrey this season, since he celebrated his 30th birthday this summer. It's also why if you have an in-prime running back, you would much rather trade them too soon than too late, since their value could be non-existent with the latter.

Young quarterbacks, on the other hand, should get a big boost for their ability to stick around. Aaron Rodgers is a starting NFL quarterback at 42 years old. Matthew Stafford is a fantasy asset at 38. If you hitch your wagon to the right young signal-caller, that's a connection you could realistically keep for a decade-plus.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson Beats Shedeur Sanders in Browns' QB1 Battle for NFL Week 1 vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders will begin his second season in the NFL on the bench for the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
Shedeur Sanders will begin his second season in the NFL on the bench for the Cleveland Browns.

Deshaun Watson was named the team's starter over Sanders on Monday for the Sept. 13 season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added that Watson was the "favorite going into camp" ahead of Sanders and Dillon Gabriel.

The quarterback battle between Sanders and Watson was the biggest storyline surrounding the Browns during OTAs and training camp, and the veteran ended up showing new head coach Todd Monken enough to win the job.

During the early portion of OTAs in May, Monken told reporters he hoped to have a quarterback depth chart in place by training camp but also did not want to rush things. He added, "we'll have it set for Jacksonville."

Yet there were signs Watson was gradually pulling away as training camp progressed:

Watson also started the preseason opener against the Chicago Bears and played solidly while going 11-of-15 for 126 yards, zero touchdowns and zero interceptions. Sanders entered the game after him and struggled while going 6-of-11 for 79 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception.

It was Sanders who played better in the second preseason game against the Buffalo Bills by going 9-of-11 for 74 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Watson was just 5-of-12 for 36 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception.

Watson then slammed Browns fans for booing him in the aftermath:

After all the back-and-forth, the depth chart is now set for Jacksonville. That means Sanders will have to wait for the chance to improve on his rookie-year struggles.

Cleveland selected him with a fifth-round pick in the 2025 NFL draft after he surprisingly fell so far despite being the Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year in his final collegiate season. He began his rookie campaign on the bench but eventually got the opportunity to start.

While his 3-4 record in seven starts doesn't exactly jump out, the Browns were 2-8 in their other 10 games. But it's not as if Sanders led the way to that improvement with excellent individual play, as he finished with seven touchdown passes, 10 interceptions and an ugly 18.9 QBR .

Still, he flashed his potential at times and played through the inconsistency that many rookies deal with in their first NFL season. He figured to be better in 2026 with a potential second-year leap, but that will be more difficult now from a backup role.

As for Watson, the Browns certainly hope he moves past the disappointment that has defined his tenure with the team.

There was a time when he was one of the best quarterbacks in the league when he made three straight Pro Bowls for the Houston Texans from 2018-20. He also led the entire NFL with 4,823 passing yards in 2020.

Yet he has made just 19 starts since the Browns traded for him before the 2022 season due to a combination of suspension and injuries. He is 9-10 in those starts and is yet to throw for more than seven touchdowns in a single season with Cleveland.

The 2026 campaign is set to be the final one on Watson's contract with the AFC North team. Winning the starting job gives him and the Browns a chance to salvage something after the team gave up draft capital in his acquisition and then gave him a five-year, fully guaranteed $230 million deal.

But this means Sanders will have to wait for his next chance.

On Monday, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that veteran Deshaun Watson has been named the Browns' starter for their Sept. 13 season opener against the Jacksonville Jaguars, beating out second-year signal-caller Shedeur Sanders.

Shedeur's Reaction to Browns' QB Decision

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that Cleveland's decision "truly came down to the end," and the team ultimately "leaned toward Watson's experience." Schultz went on to add that Watson "will have to continue earning" his starting role once the 2026 season officially starts.

Still, some are questioning the Browns' decision after watching Sanders and Watson in Saturday's 31-7 preseason loss against the Buffalo Bills. Sanders went 9-of-11 for 74 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Watson was just 5-of-12 for 36 yards and a pick. Watson also drew some attention after the game when he slammed Cleveland fans for booing him while he was on the field.

Before Cleveland's decision on Monday, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noted that Sanders had a different air around him than Watson.

"I will say about Shedeur Sanders, when I talk to people with the Browns, the word 'presence,' the word 'aura,' comes up," Fowler said on Sunday's episode of SportsCenter . "Like he has something to him that has certainly helped his cause."

In the end, the Browns chose experience over aura, and they will be hoping that Watson can prove that they made the right choice by having Sanders start the year as their backup quarterback.
