articles.title: Examining Fantasy Football 2026 Expert Mock Drafts After Preseason Week 2
articles.summary: Week 2 of the 2026 NFL preseason is finished, which can only mean one thing: We have entered peak mock draft season.
articles.body:
Week 2 of the 2026 NFL preseason is finished, which can only mean one thing: We have entered peak mock draft season.

Fantasy football managers and experts alike are racing to finalize their draft preparations, and mocking the real thing is a big part of the process.

While you can (and should) seek out mock drats with fellow enthusiasts, it's also worth perusing the mock picks from industry experts. Which is exactly what we're here to do while breaking down recent mock drafts from ESPN , Yahoo Sports and Rotoworld .

The ESPN crew compiled this mock, and things got interesting right from the start. Christian McCaffrey cracked the top five as the fourth overall pick, while Puka Nacua lasted all the way to the eighth. McCaffrey is clearly talented enough to justify such an early pick, but that's still plenty of confidence expressed in a 30-year-old running back who handled 450 touches last season (playoffs included).

As is perhaps expected in expert drafts, no tight ends were touched until the middle of the second round (Trey McBride and Brock Bowers went 27th and 28th, respectively), and no quarterbacks went until the fifth (Josh Allen, 47th). Quarterbacks weren't taken again until the seventh round (Jayden Daniels, 61st; Lamar Jackson 64th; and Drake Maye, 66th).

Waiting on quarterback is almost a universal strategy at this point, and it certainly has some merit. The general thinking is that the opportunity cost of missing out on an elite ball-carrier or pass-catcher is too great to take an early quarterback, since later-round options are often plenty productive. Still, that opportunity cost diminishes when everyone avoids the position to this degree.

For those on rookie-watch duties, Jeremiyah Love nearly cracked the second round as the 22nd player (and 13th running back) off the board. The freshman class didn't make another appearance until Carnell Tate finished the sixth round as the 60th pick.

It took just three picks for this mock, supplied by Yahoo Sports, to serve up a stunner as James Cook III went third overall—and before a single receiver was taken. Cook has been a touchdown machine the last two seasons (32 scores combined), but he lacks a great safety net if he can't keep finding the end zone, especially in this format, since he plays a small part in the passing game.

Because Cook distorted the draft board, it was hard not to like every receiver pick in the first round: Nacua at No. 4, Ja'Marr Chase at No. 5, Jaxon Smith-Njigba at No. 7, Amon-Ra St. Brown at No. 8 and CeeDee Lamb at No. 10. The receiving values carried over to the second round with Justin Jefferson sliding to No. 15 and Drake London going at No. 17.

The real intrigue from Round 2, though, came from the final picks: namely, Brock Bowers (No. 21) over Trey McBride (No. 24) and Kyren Williams (No. 23) going in the round. The Bowers-McBride debate is a fierce one, and there are arguments for both sides, but McBride still gets the edge in the majority of mocks. And the Williams' pick is a big gamble with Blake Corum breathing down his neck.

Finishing Round 3, that's where the first quarterback (Josh Allen, No. 27) and first rookie (Jeremiyah Love, No. 27) went. It also featured a couple of intriguing breakout backs near the end of the round in Javonte Williams (No. 34) and Emeka Egbuka (No. 35). Williams seems like he could handle a ton of carries, and Egbuka could feast on targets (provided, of course, that this toe sprain doesn't linger).

This Rotoworld-hosted expert mock tasked Zachary Krueger with selecting their most and least favorite picks from each manager. There were a number of interesting selections there.

Krueger, for instance, tabbed a ninth-round investment from Rotoworld's Rivers McCown in De'Zhaun Stribling as their best pick. "It feels like there is plenty of room for rookie De'Zhaun Stribling to make an impact for the 49ers this season, and the early camp reports on the rookie have been growing," Krueger wrote.

Conversely, Krueger was not a fan of fellow popular sleeper pick Wan'Dale Robinson going two picks after Stribling. "Even for all the targets that Robinson has seen over the last two years, he's finished as a top-24 PPR receiver in just 27 percent of his games, with his average PPR finish on a per game basis coming in as the WR38."

While a number of sleepers surfaced as favorite picks, Krueger did cite a third-round pick of Malik Nabers as a wise investment. "If he were cleared for full contact tomorrow, Nabers' ADP would likely propel into the late-first/early-second round," Krueger wrote. Nabers, for the record, could be getting that clearance soon .

A lot of mid-to-late fliers were cited as least favorites, but a fourth-round investment in Mike Evans (interestingly, made by the same manager who took Stribling) made the list. "Evans is a player I've been out on all offseason, largely because of last year's injury troubles and the fact that he isn't getting any younger," Krueger wrote. "In addition to those concerns, Evans also totaled 34 or fewer receiving yards in five of the eight games he played last season, and he averaged a career-low 1.2 YAC/REC."

articles.title: Justin Jefferson Drops Super Confident Quote amid Battle for No. 1 Spot in NFL WR Rankings
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings star wide receiver Justin Jefferson is willing to acknowledge that he's no longer viewed as the best player at his position, but he's confident that he will be able to reverse that perception this year.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings star wide receiver Justin Jefferson is willing to acknowledge that he's no longer viewed as the best player at his position, but he's confident that he will be able to reverse that perception this year.

Per The Athletic's Michael Silver , Jefferson said he knows he's not considered the No. 1 wide receiver in the NFL, but that will change soon.

"Not yet. Not yet," Jefferson said. "But they will (know) after this year — I'll tell you that."

Despite achieving his sixth straight 1,000-yard season, Jefferson wasn't selected to the Pro Bowl for just the second time in his career. He was limited to a career-low two touchdowns amid a disappointing year for the Vikings that was marred by subpar quarterback play.

Things are looking up for Jefferson entering the 2026 campaign, as two-time Pro Bowler Kyler Murray was named Minnesota's starting quarterback after signing with the team this offseason. Having a reliable signal-caller under center should help the 2022 NFL Offensive Player of the Year return to his usual dominant form.

Jefferson will try to back up his confidence when the Vikings open the 2026 season on Sept. 13 against the Green Bay Packers.
